subject: Follow-up: DPA clarifications & residency — BrightPath pilot
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@brightpath.health>, Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@brightpath.health>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: DPA clarifications & residency — BrightPath pilot

Hi Emma / Oliver —

Quick follow-up from our call this morning — great conversation and appreciate the clear residency + compliance priorities you shared. I summarized the items we agreed to confirm and the proposed next steps below so we can keep the pilot on a tight timeline.

Key items you asked us to confirm:
- Controller vs processor for the pilot data: you asked us to state Redwood's position in writing.
- Subprocessor notifications and list cadence: you requested a monthly list and confirmation of notification timing for any new subprocessors.
- Breach notice timing: clarified what Redwood will commit to for customer notification.
- PII handling, retention windows, and log access: you requested how long request logs and model logs are retained and what PII minimization steps we take.
- Data residency: BrightPath needs EU-only processing for the pilot (data must not leave EU).

Immediate attachments:
- [Attachment: BrightPath_DPA_draft_20280830.pdf (PDF, 124 KB)] — your DPA draft with inline redlines from the call.
- [Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary-2028.pdf (PDF, 68 KB)] — SOC 2 snapshot we pulled for quick review.

Proposed answers / clarifications from Redwood (draft — legal to confirm):
1) Role: Redwood would be the processor for customer-provided patient data in the hosted API; BrightPath is the controller. We can call out specific exceptions if BrightPath requests Redwood to perform analytics on aggregated telemetry where Redwood acts as a controller for internal ops data.
2) Breach notification: our standard commitment is to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that materially affects customer data; we will provide a preliminary notification sooner if we have firm indicators.
3) Subprocessors: we publish a current list and can provide a monthly export; for new subprocessors we propose to notify customers within 30 days of onboarding and include the subprocessor's SOC/ISO evidence where available.
4) Retention / logs: request/response logs retained by default for 30 days for troubleshooting; aggregated usage metrics retained 2 years. PII minimization: we recommend prompt-side redaction and provide guidance; we also support redaction hooks for private deployments.
5) Data residency: hosted API currently routes requests to the nearest regional cluster. For strict EU-only processing we recommended either a Dedicated/Private deployment in eu-west or a contractual residency addendum (subject to capacity and Dedicated contract).

Next steps I propose this week:
- Legal (Rishi) to confirm the language above and provide final DPA redlines.
- Mina to upload formal answers into the HubSpot deal and shared Drive link.
- Schedule a technical follow-up (solutions engineer) to scope options for EU-only processing and private deployment timelines — can you share available windows next week?

If any of the bullets above are off, please flag and I will update.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this pilot forward.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148

From: Emma Clark <emma.clark@brightpath.health>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@brightpath.health>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2028 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA clarifications & residency — BrightPath pilot

Thanks Mina — that summary is helpful. A couple clarifying asks from our side before legal reviews your redlines:  

1) Controller/processor: BrightPath will be the controller for PHI we send to the service. Please confirm in writing that Redwood will act as a processor for that PHI (including caching/KV) in the hosted API. If there are any components where Redwood is a controller, please call them out (we expect any telemetry retained for platform ops to be Redwood-controlled).

2) Breach notification: 72 hours is reasonable, but our security team prefers an initial notification within 24 hours if possible (even if preliminary). Can Redwood do an initial heads-up within 24 hours and a full incident report by 72 hours?

3) Subprocessors: monthly list is good. Will you commit to providing security evidence for any new subprocessor (SOC 2 or equivalent) in the onboarding notification?  "Available where possible" creates risk for us — we need a more definitive statement.

4) Data residency: BrightPath's legal requirement is EU-only processing for the pilot dataset. We cannot accept routing to US clusters for any of the PHI fields. If Redwood cannot guarantee EU-hosted processing on hosted API we need a firm statement and timeline for Dedicated/Private options (including estimated lead time and costs).

5) Retention: can you confirm whether logs that contain request text are ever used for model training? We need explicit confirmation that BrightPath request content will not be used for model training or to improve models.

We appreciate the attachments; Oliver and I will review and get back with specific redlines. Can Rishi or Laura weigh in on the bullet points above so we can avoid churn?

—Emma
Emma Clark
Head of Security & Privacy, BrightPath Health
emma.clark@brightpath.health | +44 20 7946 0881

Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: DPA clarifications & residency — BrightPath pilot

Rishi / Laura — forwarding BrightPath's clarifying asks (below) from Emma. Quick thoughts from AE perspective below each item — please turn into firm language we can send back to the customer.

Emma's asks:
1) Confirm Redwood is processor for PHI in hosted API.
  - AE note: we should be explicit and avoid edge-case language. Customer will push.
2) Initial incident heads-up within 24 hours + full report by 72 hours.
  - AE note: we currently do 72-hour confirmed notification; we can push initial heads-up if we have credible indicators but need legal sign-off.
3) Subprocessor evidence: commit to sending SOC2/ISO evidence for new subprocessors in onboarding notice.
  - AE note: we publish subprocessor list monthly and often have SOC2 reports; verify whether we can commit to providing evidence in all cases.
4) EU-only processing guarantee on hosted API for PHI fields or clear Dedicated timeline + costs.
  - AE note: likely only feasible with Dedicated/Private; need clear timeline estimates and pricing guidance to share.
5) Confirmation that BrightPath content will NOT be used for model training.
  - AE note: this is a common ask; we should be able to state training exclusions for customer data — legal to confirm exact language.

Proposed next actions for legal reply: please turn the above into customer-ready bullets and indicate any limitations/required contract language. Also flag anything we should escalate to product/infra (e.g., EU-hosting capacity).

Thanks — I can schedule a short sync if that helps (15–20m).

Best,
Mina

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Clark <emma.clark@brightpath.health>, Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@brightpath.health>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA clarifications & residency — BrightPath pilot

Thanks Mina — and thanks Emma for the clear asks. Below are firm positions Redwood can commit to now; where we need to add nuance it is noted. Please treat these as customer-facing language we can add to the DPA for the pilot.

1) Role (Controller/Processor): Redwood will act as a processor with respect to BrightPath’s customer-provided PHI and other customer data processed via the hosted API for the pilot. Separately, Redwood may process telemetry and platform operational data as a controller for its own operational purposes; such telemetry will be described and scoped in the DPA.

2) Incident notification: Redwood commits to the following timeline for incidents materially affecting BrightPath data: (a) preliminary notification — initial heads-up within 24 hours of our becoming aware of a confirmed indicator that meets our incident triage threshold; (b) follow-up with a substantive incident report and remedial plan within 72 hours of confirmation. We will include available forensic detail in the 72-hour report and provide updates as investigation progresses.

3) Subprocessor onboarding and evidence: Redwood will provide a monthly export of current subprocessors. For any newly onboarded subprocessor, Redwood will notify BrightPath within 30 days of onboarding. Redwood will include available security evidence (SOC 2 / ISO / security questionnaire responses) with the onboarding notice. If evidence is not yet available at the time of notice, Redwood will share progress milestones and a target date for evidence delivery.

4) Data residency / EU-only processing: Redwood hosted API routes requests to regional clusters and cannot guarantee EU-only processing for hosted multi-tenant endpoints at this time. For a contractual guarantee of EU-only processing for PHI, Redwood proposes either: (a) Dedicated capacity in eu-west with contractual residency addendum (lead time typically 6–10 weeks once a Dedicated contract is signed), or (b) Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment. Mina: solutions engineering to provide cost/lead-time estimates for both options; we will not commit to EU-only processing on hosted shared infrastructure for this pilot.

5) Use for training: Redwood confirms BrightPath request content and PHI will not be used to train production models or incorporated into model improvement pipelines unless explicit written consent is provided. This exclusion will be reflected in the DPA.

6) Retention and logs: Default request logs retained 30 days; aggregated usage metrics retained 2 years. We will provide access logs and audit evidence on request as part of the pilot operational support.

Next steps (to keep pilot moving):
- Mina to send this language back to BrightPath and attach revised DPA draft.
- Solutions engineering (cc Mina) to create an options memo for Dedicated vs Private residency (cost + ETA).
- If BrightPath wants a binding residency commitment, we will require a Dedicated/Private order and typical lead time.

If Emma/Oliver are comfortable with the language above I will prepare a redlined DPA showing these commitments and send via DocuSign for signature.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0210
